prompt: Use a compact constructor to clean up a warehouse shelf tag: trim and upper-case the sku, trim the aisle, and turn negative quantities into 0. Complete the ShelfTag record, then run the tests.
explanation: A compact constructor names no parameters and no body assignments: you simply reassign the implicit parameters, and the record then stores those cleaned-up values in its fields. Normalising there means every instance is valid no matter how it was built, so equals and hashCode -- which records generate from the stored components -- treat "  ab-12 " and "ab-12" as the same tag. label() is an ordinary instance method that reads the already-normalised accessors.
hints: The compact constructor is written as `public ShelfTag { ... }` -- no parameter list and no `this.sku = ...` line.
Inside it, assign straight to the parameter names: `sku = sku.trim().toUpperCase();` after handling the null case.
label() can just concatenate the accessors: sku() + " @ " + aisle() + " x" + quantity().
